skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate and edit AI videos through the inference.sh CLI using models such as Veo, Seedance, Wan, Grok, OmniHuman, and Fabric.
skill.summary: Create text-to-video, image-to-video, avatar, lipsync, upscaling, and foley workflows through the inference.sh CLI.
skill.author: inference-sh-9

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown code fences, inline model identifiers, documentation links, or placeholder media URLs. One critical issue is confirmed: the quick start uses curl piped directly to sh to install a remote CLI before login.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl to sh with manual download steps, checksum verification, and a separate execution command.

remediation.issue: The quick start mixes installation and login in one shell command.
remediation.suggestion: Show installation, verification, and login as separate steps so users can inspect each action.

remediation.issue: The skill includes external image and documentation URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer marketplace-hosted media or clearly label external links before users open them.

content.value_statement: Video creation often requires many separate tools and model choices. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code run inference.sh video workflows from clear prompts.
actual_capabilities: Lists inference.sh video models for text-to-video, image-to-video, avatars, lipsync, foley, and upscaling.
Shows infsh commands for Veo, Grok, Seedance, Wan, OmniHuman, Fabric, PixVerse, Topaz, and media merger apps.
Provides prompt and input patterns for generating videos from text descriptions.
Provides input patterns for animating images and adding audio-driven lipsync.
Links to inference.sh documentation for running apps, streaming results, and content pipelines.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated inference.sh account.
Depends on external inference.sh services and model availability.
Does not create videos offline or include model weights.
Generated media quality, cost, and runtime vary by selected model.

use_cases.title: Create Social Clips
use_cases.description: Generate short video concepts from text prompts for social channels and campaign tests.

use_cases.title: Prototype Product Demos
use_cases.description: Turn product images or scripts into quick animated clips for review before production.

use_cases.title: Build Avatar Videos
use_cases.description: Create talking head or lipsync workflows from a portrait and narration audio.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short AI video about [scene]. Use a fast inference.sh video model and explain the command before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Animate an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use inference.sh to animate this image URL: [image URL]. Make the motion [motion style] and keep the result suitable for [channel].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Talking Avatar
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a talking avatar video from [portrait URL] and [audio URL]. Pick the best listed model and describe the expected output.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Video Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an inference.sh workflow that generates a video, adds foley sound, upscales it, and merges it with [other clips].

output_examples.input: Create a five second beach sunset video with waves and ambient motion.
output_examples.output: A selected fast text-to-video model, a concise prompt, and a ready-to-run inference.sh command.

output_examples.input: Animate a product photo and add subtle camera movement for a launch teaser.
output_examples.output: An image-to-video model choice, motion guidance, and notes about expected resolution and runtime.

output_examples.input: Make a training presenter speak from a portrait and narration file.
output_examples.output: A recommended avatar or lipsync app, required media inputs, and a command outline for the workflow.

best_practices: Install and verify the inference.sh CLI before using model commands.
Use clear scene, motion, duration, and style details in video prompts.
Check model costs, resolution limits, and content policies before long runs.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote install scripts into a shell without local verification.
Do not use private images, voices, or faces without permission.
Do not assume one model is best for every video workflow.

faq.question: Does this skill generate video directly inside the assistant?
faq.answer: No. It helps the assistant run inference.sh CLI workflows that call hosted video models.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create videos from images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes image-to-video examples using models such as Wan and Seedance.

faq.question: Can it create lipsync or avatar videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse workflows for avatar and lipsync use cases.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on the inference.sh CLI and hosted model APIs.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The quick start uses a remote installer piped to a shell. Users should verify downloads before running them.
